product.olivetti-pcs11.summary: Compact 1992 desktop with a 16 MHz 386SX, aimed at home and small-business users.
product.olivetti-pcs11.history: Olivetti introduced the PCS 11 in November 1992, together with the PCS 33 and PCS 44, as part of a compact series designed to be easy to use. It was the cheapest of the three and took up no more desk space than an A4 sheet. It was aimed at home and small-business users: 16 MHz 386SX, 2 MB of memory, a 40 MB hard disk and a 1.44 MB floppy drive, with MS-DOS 5.0 and Windows 3.0 preinstalled. Inside it uses the BA013/16 board, the same technical base as the M300-02, but with its own BIOS (R2.04 and R2.07).
product.olivetti-pcs11.technical.verifie: BIOS R2.04 and R2.07 (128 KB) are identified and can be selected in the machine configuration. Booting has been observed.
product.olivetti-pcs11.technical.limitat: Bootable partial emulation. Its BIOS differs from the PCS 33 one only in the memory and bus timings it programs into the TOPCAT chipset, which the emulator does not use. The case is not modelled. Other memory sizes, the hard disk and more software remain to be tested.
No hard disk: one 1.44 MB floppy drive
product.olivetti-pcs11.creation.model: 1992 PCS 11: 16 MHz 386SX, 2 MB, integrated WD90C11 and one 1.44 MB floppy drive
product.olivetti-pcs11.creation.note: This board’s BIOS supports only four drive types. If you add the disk, choose the type shown in the option in Setup. The disk connects to the board’s IDE interface.
product.olivetti-pcs11.technical.cpu: 16 MHz Intel 386SX on the BA013/16 board, with an i387SX socket. VLSI TOPCAT chipset: VL82C320 system controller and VL82C331 bus controller. Two 16-bit ISA slots on the bus expansion board. Data taken from the BA013 board shared with the M300-02/02F; there is no PCS service guide.
product.olivetti-pcs11.technical.memory: Bank 0 with 2 MB soldered and bank 1 with two sockets for 1 M × 9 SIMMs (2 MB in total) or 4 M × 9 SIMMs (8 MB in total): 2, 4 or 10 MB. 80 ns access.
product.olivetti-pcs11.technical.video: Integrated VGA: Western Digital WD90C11A, WD90C64 clock generator and Brooktree BT476 DAC. BluMach uses its WD90C11 model with 512 KB.
product.olivetti-pcs11.technical.storage: 3.5-inch 1.44 MB or 5.25-inch 1.2 MB floppy drive, with an Acer controller and serial and parallel ports in the 87C310. The IDE disk uses a buffered interface on the board. The BIOS table has only four types; the first three are 965/5/17 (40 MB), 975/10/17 (85 MB) and 761/8/39 (120 MB).
product.olivetti-pcs11.technical.firmwar: BIOS R2.04 (06/03/92) and R2.07 (03/01/93), 128 KB each, are preserved. Their disk table has the same four types as the M300-02 one, with slightly different geometries.
product.olivetti-pcs11.technical.commerc: Introduced in November 1992 with 2 MB, a 40 MB hard disk, a 1.44 MB floppy drive, MS-DOS 5.0 and Windows 3.0.
product.olivetti-pcs11.technical.press: Computer Business Review, 15/11/1992: launch of the PCS 11, PCS 33 and PCS 44.
product.olivetti-pcs11.warning: IN DEVELOPMENT: we are working on the PCS 11 emulation. You can create the machine, but it may fail or stop partway. Any result you send us, even if it does not boot, helps us finish it.
